editorial.headline: Chemical Packaging: Open Nationally, Unblocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 82924 covers paid or contracted chemical-material and product packaging—open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 82924 is the business of packaging chemical materials and products for a fee or under contract. It is not confined to one package format or one way of working. The scope expressly includes automatic and manual processes, from bottling liquids to packing solid articles using blister packaging or aluminium-foil wrapping. It also includes secure packaging for chemical materials and products, labelling, stamping, sterilising products and other work connected with their packaging. The practical centre of gravity is the packaging service itself: the defined work of preparing chemical materials and products in the stated forms.

That breadth matters because the activity can encompass bottling, enclosure of solid items and finishing steps that identify a package through labels or stamps, or subject products to sterilisation. It can be undertaken with equipment-driven processes or manually, as the scope itself allows. The record opens registration at every listed scale—Micro, Small, Medium and Large. In other words, the scale field does not reserve this activity for a narrow band of enterprises; each of the four listed scales is open.

The national PMA position is equally direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and its maximum foreign ownership is 100. That means the national ceiling permits full foreign ownership; it is not an opening that stops short of complete foreign participation. The record names Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the PMA source. For a founder considering this defined packaging activity at the national level, the fact to retain is simple but significant: the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, alongside access across the record’s full range of scales.

Bali needs to be read on its own terms rather than assumed from the national result. The provincial moratorium in the record permanently blocks PMA registration, island-wide, for Low and Medium-Low risk classifications. Yet this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali reason records that, at the Large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High and that it is not blocked by the moratorium. The record’s status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The honest Bali conclusion is therefore open, not closed: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. Large-scale work carries the stated Medium-High/High OSS-risk position, but it remains outside the moratorium’s blocked Low and Medium-Low categories.
